sources.name: OS Terrain 50 Overview
sources.role: Terrain 50 product resolution, update, format and published-accuracy contract
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 is a lower-resolution digital terrain model intended for landscape visualisation and analysis over large areas.
Its grid uses regular 50 metre post spacing and its contour product uses 10 metre intervals.
Ordnance Survey states that OS Terrain 50 grid data has been verified to 4 metre RMSE.
semantic_limits: The 4 metre RMSE and 50 metre spacing make Terrain 50 a screening cross-check rather than a replacement for EA DTM 1 metre parcel sampling.
Product-level accuracy is not parcel-specific measurement certification.
A product overview does not prove that the exact tile bytes used by the runner were downloaded and sampled.

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 Technical Specification
sources.role: Terrain 50 tile, grid, contour and supply-format contract
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 grid and contour products are supplied as 10 kilometre by 10 kilometre tiles.
The grid is available with 50 metre post spacing in ASCII grid and GML 3.2.1.
Grid and contour products are created from the same source data.
semantic_limits: Shared source lineage does not make grid and contour representations numerically interchangeable.
A 10 kilometre tile identifier is spatial addressing evidence, not exact parcel geometry.
Format availability does not establish complete-object retrieval or valid-pixel sampling.

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 Grid Data
sources.role: ASCII grid dimensions, pixel-centre height and GML metadata contract
verified_facts: Each Terrain 50 grid tile is represented by 200 rows of 200 pixels at 50 metre cell size.
Height values are calculated from the centre of each pixel and are published to the nearest 0.1 metre.
The GML file supplies location, spacing, vertical-reference and spatial-reference metadata for the ASCII data.
semantic_limits: Published decimal precision is not equivalent to vertical accuracy.
The GML metadata file does not replace hashing and validating the external ASCII height block.
Pixel-centre values must not be treated as exact values at arbitrary parcel vertices.

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 Data Structure
sources.role: Terrain 50 raster-cell, tile-edge and interpolated spot-height semantics contract
verified_facts: Terrain 50 grid heights are calculated at pixel centres.
Tiles do not share common edge values because of the raster construction method.
Spot heights are selected from an interpolated surface and are not guaranteed to be summits or the highest point of a feature.
semantic_limits: Tile-edge discontinuity checks must not assume duplicated border posts.
An interpolated spot height is not a substitute for exact raster-cell sampling inside a parcel polygon.
Visual agreement at tile boundaries is not numeric acceptance evidence.

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 Source Data
sources.role: TIN source, interpolation, bare-earth modelling and datum context contract
verified_facts: The Terrain source DTM is captured as a triangulated irregular network using mass points and breaklines.
Terrain 50 grid and contours are interpolated from the source TIN.
The source records bare-earth terrain and generally excludes buildings, supported structures and vegetation.
semantic_limits: Interpolation from a TIN can smooth local extrema and must remain a coarse cross-check.
Bare-earth modelling rules do not prove that every local object was classified perfectly.
Source-model description does not replace exact tile provenance and datum receipts.

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 Metadata
sources.role: Per-tile GEMINI metadata, product identification and tile-reference contract
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 provides XML metadata following the GEMINI metadata standard.
Metadata is available on a per-tile basis.
The metadata includes product identification, spatial representation and the 10 kilometre National Grid tile reference.
semantic_limits: Metadata presence is provenance context rather than numeric elevation evidence.
A tile-reference field must be checked against the actual downloaded object and parcel location.
Metadata completeness does not establish payload-byte completeness.

sources.name: OS Terrain 5 Grid Data
sources.role: Terrain 5 pixel-mean, 5 metre grid and external-data-block semantics contract
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 grid heights represent the mean height across each 5 metre pixel.
Each 5 kilometre tile contains 1000 rows of 1000 pixels.
The GML file supplies metadata while the spatial height values are held in the external ASCII grid block.
semantic_limits: A 5 metre pixel mean is a different statistic from the EA 1 metre maximum-minus-minimum parcel metric.
GML parsing alone does not prove that the corresponding ASCII values were read.
Terrain 5 remains secondary QA and must not overwrite EA DTM 1 metre results.

sources.name: INSPIRE GML Technical Guidance
sources.role: Native British National Grid polygon and reprojection-risk contract
verified_facts: HM Land Registry supplies INSPIRE polygons in GML.
The polygon data is captured against British National Grid.
HM Land Registry warns that conversion from British National Grid to WGS84 can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
semantic_limits: WGS84 display coordinates must not replace native EPSG:27700 geometry for exact containment.
INSPIRE index polygons are indicative extents and are not legal-boundary determinations.
Successful reprojection does not establish parcel identity or elevation accuracy.

sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) - 1m
sources.role: Primary DTM product, resolution, lineage, tiling, datum and accuracy contract
verified_facts: The Environment Agency DTM is a 1 metre raster elevation model covering approximately 99 percent of England.
It combines time-stamped and National LIDAR Programme surveys, using newer and better-resolution data where repeat surveys exist.
It is supplied as 5 kilometre GeoTIFF tiles in metres, referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn with OSTN15, and individual surveys have plus or minus 15 centimetre RMSE.
semantic_limits: Composite coverage can contain surveys from different dates, so per-location metadata remains required.
The product accuracy statement is not a guarantee for every pixel or parcel.
A dataset landing page is not proof that the exact GeoTIFF bytes were downloaded and processed.

sources.name: Survey Data Catalogue - Vertical Accuracy of LiDAR Data
sources.role: Absolute and relative LiDAR error-budget contract
verified_facts: Environment Agency specifications require absolute height error below plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
The absolute error is assessed against Ground Truth Survey data.
Environment Agency expects relative random height error to be no more than plus or minus 5 centimetres.
semantic_limits: Specification thresholds are uncertainty inputs, not parcel-specific certification.
Relative error must not be conflated with absolute vertical datum error.
The thresholds do not validate an unexecuted sampling pipeline.

sources.name: Survey Data Catalogue - Projection Information
sources.role: OSGB36, ODN, OSTN15 and historical geoid lineage contract
verified_facts: Environment Agency survey data is supplied in OSGB36 British National Grid with elevations above Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
The LiDAR Composite uses OSTN15.
Post-26 August 2016 surveys use OSGM15, while older time-stamped surveys require metadata-specific geoid identification.
semantic_limits: Historical surveys must not be silently mixed across transformation or geoid generations.
Horizontal transformation correctness does not establish vertical surface accuracy.
Datum metadata is provenance evidence and does not replace raster-value validation.

sources.name: Survey Data Catalogue - LiDAR Data Metadata
verified_facts: Environment Agency provides downloadable index catalogues for LiDAR products.
The catalogues include details such as the time of year when data was collected.
The metadata supports identifying survey lineage for a location.
semantic_limits: Metadata availability is not numeric elevation evidence.
A catalogue row must remain bound to the exact raster tile and location.
Collection-time metadata does not prove current source freshness without a readback.

sources.name: National LIDAR Programme
sources.role: National programme coverage, phase and publication-lineage contract
verified_facts: The National LIDAR Programme provides 1 metre elevation data for all of England.
Phase 1 survey blocks were captured between January 2017 and February 2023.
Repeat surveys receive incrementing phase numbers and data is published through the Defra survey portal on an ongoing quarterly basis.
semantic_limits: National coverage does not mean all locations have the same survey date or phase.
Programme metadata does not identify the exact survey used at a parcel without location-specific lineage.
Quarterly publication does not prove that a cached local object is the latest version.

sources.name: OGC GeoPackage Encoding Standard 1.4.0
sources.role: SQLite geospatial container, feature, tile and integrity-constraint contract
verified_facts: GeoPackage defines rules for storing vector features, imagery or raster map tile matrices and non-spatial tables in SQLite.
Version 1.4.0 is identified as OGC document 12-128r19.
The standard defines table schemas, integrity assertions, limitations and content constraints.
semantic_limits: Container conformance does not establish source authority or elevation semantics.
A tile table or feature table is not proof that every referenced payload was validated.
Database integrity must not be promoted to parcel-height accuracy.

sources.name: Common Query Language (CQL2) 1.0
sources.role: Text and JSON filter-grammar and subset-selection contract
verified_facts: CQL2 is a generic filter grammar for selecting a subset of resource instances from a source collection.
The standard defines both text and JSON encodings.
CQL2 can be used in query operations and in other operations such as updates.
semantic_limits: A successful filter identifies a selected subset and does not prove complete-source examination.
A true spatial predicate does not establish authoritative parcel identity or numeric elevation.
Filter parsing and execution must not create business rows without source, geometry and measurement receipts.

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.name: FIPS 180-4 Secure Hash Standard
sources.role: SHA message-digest and post-digest change-detection contract
verified_facts: FIPS 180-4 specifies secure hash algorithms used to generate message digests.
The digests can be used to detect whether messages changed after digest generation.
The August 2015 publication supersedes the March 2012 FIPS 180-4 publication.
semantic_limits: A matching digest establishes byte identity only for the exact hashed object and algorithm.
Hash equality does not prove publisher authority, semantic correctness or measurement accuracy.
A digest must remain bound to acquisition time, source identity and execution receipts.
